claims.text: A thin, continuous, adherent Al2O3 coating on cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will improve oxidation resistance at 1000 °C in air for exposures up to 100 hours.
The Al2O3 coating will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion into HfNbTaTiZr.
Preventing oxygen diffusion into HfNbTaTiZr will inhibit the formation of harmful oxides.
Inhibiting harmful oxide formation will reduce oxidation-induced degradation.
Reduced oxidation-induced degradation will preserve the alloy's mechanical properties.
After exposure at 1000 °C in air, coated HfNbTaTiZr will maintain a yield strength above 163 MPa.
After exposure at 1000 °C in air, coated HfNbTaTiZr will have tensile ductility above 8%.
The coated alloy will show minimal mechanical-performance change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The claimed mechanical-performance retention applies at strain rates of 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1 and temperatures up to 1000 °C.
Coating effectiveness may depend on coating thickness, uniformity, and adhesion.
The coating process and substrate surface preparation may affect coating uniformity and adhesion.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says mechanical performance will not be compromised and predicts only minimal change, but the falsification rule permits decreases of up to 20% in yield strength or tensile ductility without falsifying the hypothesis.
